output.reply: Two new sources bear on NVDA, one for and one against. Cloud companies say demand to run models, not only train them, is a main reason they order accelerators, and one large cloud company says it now runs more of its own work on chips it designs. The second source strengthens the point already on your card and bears on your wrong-if condition. How much of NVDA's revenue comes from that company is not disclosed.

findings.fact: Cloud companies said demand to run AI models, not only to train them, is now a main reason they order accelerators.
One large cloud company said it now runs more of its own AI work on chips it designs itself.
If running models keeps driving orders, accelerator demand may not depend only on training; this is inference from one news report, not a disclosed figure.
A buyer shifting more work to its own chips is the condition your wrong-if option names; the size of that buyer's share of Nvidia revenue is not disclosed in these sources.
